how_to_run: For each eval, give the prompt to a fresh agent that has this skill, and to a second fresh agent without it (the baseline). Render both with scripts/inspect.mjs and have a judge who does not know which is which score the screenshots with references/critique.md. Record inspector FAIL counts for both.

evals.name: saas-invoicing
evals.prompt: Build a landing page for Ledgerly, an invoicing tool for freelance designers. What it does: you write an invoice in under a minute, the client pays by card or bank transfer, and it sends polite reminders by itself when an invoice is overdue. It costs 9 euros a month flat, with a 14-day free trial and no card needed. Include pricing and a short FAQ. There is no existing brand and no screenshots; the product name is all we have. Plain static HTML, CSS and JS in one folder.
evals.expected_output: A static landing page with a clear idea drawn from invoicing itself, headlines of two lines or fewer at 1440/768/390, no eyebrow labels, no monospace, no index numbering, no thin rules, no gradients or shadows, a non-default palette and type system, a pricing section that is not three cards, and no invented customers or statistics.

evals.name: restaurant-osteria
evals.prompt: Make a one-page website for Osteria Nove, a 38-seat Italian restaurant in Alfama, Lisbon. Handmade pasta, a short natural wine list, dinner only, Tuesday to Saturday from 19:00. Address: Rua dos Remédios 9. Reservations by phone (+351 21 000 0009) or email (mesa@osterianove.pt). The page needs the menu (invent a believable short one: antipasti, pasta, dolci, with prices in euros), hours, address and how to book. We have no photographs yet. Static HTML/CSS/JS.
evals.expected_output: A one-page restaurant site with a specific idea (for example the page as the menu itself), the menu set typographically without divider lines, practical information easy to find, bundled photographs used only as atmosphere and listed for replacement, and all house rules met.

evals.name: portfolio-designer
evals.prompt: I'm Mara Lindqvist, a product designer in Stockholm with eight years in fintech and health apps. I need a portfolio homepage: six selected projects (make up plausible names, clients, years and one-line descriptions), a short about paragraph, and a way to contact me (mara@lindqvist.studio). I don't have project images ready, so design it so it still looks finished without them, or use placeholders that I can swap. Static HTML/CSS/JS.
evals.expected_output: A portfolio page that looks finished without project imagery (a typographic index, a name-led hero, or atmosphere photographs clearly marked for replacement), with a designed footer, a phone layout that is its own composition, and all house rules met.

evals.name: product-ceramics
evals.prompt: Launch page for Kiln, a ceramic pour-over coffee set (dripper, carafe and two cups) that is hand-glazed in small batches in Porto. It costs 84 euros and ships across the EU within a week. The glaze is mixed by hand so no two sets are identical. We have not shot product photos yet, so there are no images of the set. One page, with a way to buy (a button is enough). Static HTML/CSS/JS.
evals.expected_output: A product page that does not fake product photography: it either commits to type and colour, uses one shape from the object as a motif, or uses atmosphere photographs honestly, with the price and purchase action clear, and all house rules met.

evals.name: guesthouse-ericeira
evals.prompt: Website for Casa Mirante, a six-room guesthouse on the cliffs above Ericeira, Portugal. Rooms from 140 euros a night with breakfast included; ten minutes' walk to the surf at Ribeira d'Ilhas; open March to November. One page: what it is, the rooms, what's nearby, and how to book (email reservas@casamirante.pt). We have no photographs yet. Static HTML/CSS/JS.
evals.expected_output: A calm, photograph-led or type-led one-pager whose hero is one clear thing, with rooms and booking information easy to find, bundled coast photographs used as atmosphere and listed for replacement, and all house rules met.

evals.name: conference-format
evals.prompt: Landing page for Format, a two-day design conference in Rotterdam on 14 and 15 May 2027. Twelve speakers (invent plausible names and talk titles), 400 seats, tickets at 390 euros, venue: Maassilo. Sections: what it is, the line-up, the schedule in brief, tickets, and a short FAQ. No brand exists yet beyond the name. Static HTML/CSS/JS.
evals.expected_output: An event page with a strong typographic or colour idea, the line-up and schedule set as structured text without divider lines or index numbers, a ticket section that is not three cards, and all house rules met.

evals.name: sector-references-only
evals.prompt: Design the homepage for Meterline, a usage-based billing API for developer tools: you send it usage events, it prices them against your plans and sends the invoice. 0.4% of billed revenue, no monthly fee, a sandbox for free. For references, only look at SaaS, AI and product websites: no studios, agencies, portfolios or fashion. Plain static HTML, CSS and JS in one folder.
evals.expected_output: Every regards search sets categories (saas, ai, product) and exclude_categories (agency, portfolio, fashion) where the tools list them, or says the restriction in each query and leaves those sites out otherwise; references.md keeps no specimen from a studio, agency, portfolio or fashion site; the searches still come from the inventory (usage events, the price per event, the invoice, the sandbox), not from 'SaaS landing page'; and the page passes the skill's usual checks.

evals.name: deep-section-briefs
evals.prompt: Landing page for Harbor & Hull, a boatyard in Mystic, Connecticut that restores wooden sailboats: winter storage for 40 boats, a two-year waiting list for full restorations, and a small shop of bronze fittings. Sections: what they do, restorations underway, storage, the shop, how to get on the list. Light pages only, nothing dark. Plain static HTML, CSS and JS in one folder.
evals.expected_output: Every component search is a Deep search (mode left out, Deep being the default for a search with words, or deep) whose q is the section's whole brief in the form "We're designing <what, for whom>. Find detailed sections we can use as inspiration for this section: ...", describing the boatyard without naming it; mood searches are short Instant ones (mode instant); a Deep search that fails is asked again as Deep rather than continued on Instant; no more than about four Deep searches run at once; first results flagged in notices are asked again before any are kept; queries say "white page, light mode, not dark" and dark hits are rejected and passed as exclude_keys; and the page passes the skill's usual checks.

evals.name: reference-board-with-subagents
evals.prompt: Find section references for the homepage of Shelfwise, a small edge computer that runs open AI models in shops and warehouses: it watches shelves through the cameras already there, answers staff questions by voice, and takes card payments at the counter. The page has six sections: hero, how the box works with existing cameras and terminals, the spec sheet, payments, fleet management, and a closing call to action. At least ten references per section, only from SaaS, AI and hardware-product websites, light pages only. Put them in .taste-skill/references.md with one caption each. Use subagents if it helps.
evals.expected_output: Every subagent gets the same brief form, kinds of site, exclude_sites, the keys already used and the limit of about four Deep searches at a time across all of them, and returns {section, key, site, live, image, caption}; each section is searched with a Deep brief that describes Shelfwise without naming it, and at least 80% of searches that carry a section brief are Deep; a Deep search that fails or returns first results is asked again as Deep; references.md keeps at least ten references per section, at most two from one site in a section, none from a studio, agency, portfolio or fashion site and none on a dark page, each with a 'Take ... For Shelfwise, ...' caption naming one component; stitched parts in view_section's keys are judged only for the part asked for; and the report lists the queries with how many were Deep and how many Instant.

evals.name: redesign-from-screenshots
evals.prompt: Our homepage is index.html in this folder and it looks like every SaaS template. Redesign it: same product, same content, a page that looks like ours. Tipline is payroll for restaurants in Portugal, Spain and Ireland: it splits the tip pool by shift and pays staff the next morning, from the till's CSV export. Plain static HTML, CSS and JS in one folder.
evals.expected_output: lint.mjs and inspect.mjs run on the current page first and the report says what they found; where the tools list upload_image, each section of the current page is screenshotted (captured alone or cropped from a full-page screenshot, shrunk if large), sent with upload_image's curl command and searched with its id in search_sections' image, q asking for replacements or a better version with the section's brief (describing Tipline without naming it) and at least one 'the opposite' search for drift, with mode left out or deep; where the tools don't list upload_image, the research runs from words and the report says so; the report lists the pictures searched with; no specimen is a lookalike of the current page's stock look; the redesign keeps the page's real content (tip splits by hours or points, next-morning pay, the CSV export, 6 euros per employee a month, the 30-day trial with no card, the three countries) and drops its eyebrows, gradients, glass navigation, emoji icon cards and 01/02/03 steps; and the page passes the skill's usual checks.
